summary:
Allwork.Space reports on an OpenAI working paper finding no meaningful statistical relationship between how intensively companies use ChatGPT and their revenue per employee, undercutting the assumption that heavier AI adoption automatically yields better financial results.

Key details: the 69-page paper analyzed more than 17 million ChatGPT Enterprise messages from more than 1,500 organizations, comparing usage with company financial data while controlling for factors such as company size and industry. Revenue per employee was not meaningfully associated with either message volume per employee or AI-generated tokens used per employee.

The article frames this as significant because employers increasingly try to justify large AI investments by pointing to productivity and financial returns. Usage metrics alone do not demonstrate whether those investments pay off.

On usage patterns, AI work spanned 60 categories including writing, technical tasks, research, communication, sales, planning, legal work and data analysis. Early-career employees were among the heaviest users, sending roughly eight to nine more messages per week than the average employee at their companies, while executives used the tools less frequently.

The piece concludes that the harder question for employers is not adoption measurement but whether AI is improving the work that matters to the business. Companies will need to identify which applications produce measurable gains in productivity, quality or business performance rather than assuming volume of use converts into revenue.

claims.claim: No meaningful statistical relationship was found between company ChatGPT usage intensity and revenue per employee
The working paper analyzed a large corpus of enterprise AI messages across many organizations
claims.stat: 69-page paper; more than 17 million ChatGPT Enterprise messages from more than 1,500 organizations

claims.claim: Analysis controlled for company size and industry when comparing usage to financial data

claims.stat: roughly 8 to 9 more messages per week

claims.claim: Executives used AI less frequently than other employee groups
